children: shares climbed about 2% Tuesday even as a labor dispute at its Taiwan operations moved closer to possible strike action.

The Taoyuan union plans to hold a strike vote in early October after another round of mediation ended without an agreement. Workers are seeking a permanent compensation formula that would direct 15% of operating profit toward employee bonuses.

Micron has offered Taiwan employees a fiscal 2026 package equivalent to 35 to 68 months of pay, but union representatives have rejected a one-time reward structure in favor of recurring profit sharing. The company has said it remains willing to continue discussions.

The dispute comes as Taiwan remains a key manufacturing base for Micron's memory products, including DRAM and high-bandwidth memory used in AI systems. A prolonged work stoppage could add pressure to an already tight memory market, although there has been no reported production disruption so far.

title: Micron Stock Climbs Despite $25 Billion Plant Labor Dispute
